overview: The SBA Disaster Transparency Act would require the Small Business Administration (SBA), the federal agency that makes low-interest disaster loans to businesses and homeowners after hurricanes, floods, and other disasters, to post several of its required disaster assistance reports on its public website. Under current law, those reports go only to the House and Senate committees that oversee small business; this bill keeps that requirement and adds public posting. It does not change how disaster loans work or how much money is available. As of March 4, 2025, the Senate Small Business Committee had approved it without changes and it was placed on the Senate calendar.
for: Supporters say disaster survivors, businesses, and taxpayers should be able to see how the SBA's disaster loan program is performing without waiting for Congress to release the information.
against: Critics say the bill only changes where existing reports are posted and does nothing to speed up disaster loans or fix problems the reports may reveal.
